headline: 2 Solana token mints catalogued for Bitget SOL (BGSOL); no admin, stake-pool or authority addresses surfaced.
short_headline: 2 BGSOL mints on Solana; no control addresses

findings.text: Solscan was the only Solana explorer tried. Direct fetch of its token pages was blocked or failed. Two token mints surfaced from non-explorer pages: bgSoLfRx1wRPehwC9TyG568AGjnf1sQG1MYa8s3FbfY (Bitget's own listing announcement) and BGSo18NXTWGtyNa5DBBP1ZCfUFRPWj6bECrPKakn8qN (Solflare token page). No multisig, timelock or authority addresses surfaced.

No official 'Deployed contracts' page was found. The Bitget staking page (protocol.website) lists only generic SOL staking APRs and no addresses. The Bitget events page for BGSOL returned an empty body when fetched.
No audit links are pinned and none were found on the fetched pages. No audit PDFs were walked.
No GitHub repo is pinned and none was surfaced. No deployment artifacts were found.
Solana is the only chain. Two mints were recorded; the explorer cross-check of both failed.
No factory contracts were identified, so no children were enumerated. The read API does not support Solana.
Both addresses are classified role 'token' with actor_class 'unknown'. Bytecode and account data were not read.
Both admin_addresses entries trace to fetched URLs in evidence[]. Further sightings seen only in search snippets (Coinbase, Phantom, CoinMarketCap) were not added as new addresses.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run: walked the Bitget staking page, Bitget news posts and a Solflare token page. Catalogued 2 Solana token mints (one of them probably stale or a duplicate); no control addresses found; grade is always unknown for discovery.

evidence.shows: protocol.website is a generic Bitget SOL staking marketing page. It lists APRs and an FAQ on redemption (standard and a 10%-fee 'express' option) and contains no contract addresses. It describes Bitget-run custodial-style staking in the 'Earn' product.

Bitget's Feb 2025 listing announcement describes BGSOL as a liquid staking token developed by Bitget. It gives the Solana contract address bgSoLfRx1wRPehwC9TyG568AGjnf1sQG1MYa8s3FbfY and links to the Solscan token page and the events page https://www.bitget.com/events/bitget-sol-staking.
Solflare lists 'Bitget Staked SOL (BGSOL)' with a different Solana mint, BGSo18NXTWGtyNa5DBBP1ZCfUFRPWj6bECrPKakn8qN, marked as verified in its token registry. It reports very low liquidity.

Oct 2024 press piece: Bitget launched SOL liquid staking in partnership with Solayer, a restaking network on Solana. Stakers receive BGSOL, rewards accrue through the SOL/BGSOL exchange rate (updated every 2 to 3 days), and redemption pays out SOL within about four days.

unknowns: D1-offchain: fetch of https://solscan.io/token/bgSoLfRx1wRPehwC9TyG568AGjnf1sQG1MYa8s3FbfY failed (first attempt: allowlist rejection; later attempt: 'URL could not be accessed'). Fetch of https://solscan.io/token/BGSo18NXTWGtyNa5DBBP1ZCfUFRPWj6bECrPKakn8qN was rejected before any search surfaced it. No on-chain account data (mint authority, freeze authority, supply, program owner) was read for either mint.

D1: Which mint is canonical is unresolved. Bitget's own announcement gives bgSoLfRx1…FbfY. Wallet and aggregator pages (Solflare, Phantom, Coinbase) show BGSo18NX…n8qN. Search snippets show both mints on Coinbase pages. Supply and market-cap figures in snippets differ widely, so one may be legacy or a re-issue. Verify on-chain.

D1: Mint authority, freeze authority, the Solayer stake pool or restaking program, validator vote accounts, withdraw/stake authorities and any Bitget operator multisig are all unidentified. No Solana-specific explorer pages beyond Solscan's token URL were tried.

D2: No official deployments or addresses doc was found for Bitget SOL. The page https://www.bitget.com/events/bitget-sol-staking returned an empty body when fetched. https://www.bitget.com/support/articles/12560603836686 (staking how-to) appeared only as a search snippet and was not fetched.
D3: No audit reports were found or pinned for BGSOL or its Solayer-based infrastructure.
D4: No GitHub repo or deployment artifacts were found. protocol.github is empty and no repo was surfaced on the fetched pages.
D5: chain Solana: only the two token mints surfaced, from Bitget's news page and Solflare. No other address types surfaced.
D6: No factory contracts or pools identified. The defipunkd read API supports no Solana chainId, so no children could be enumerated.

D8: Sightings that appeared only in search snippets were not promoted to admin_addresses (no new address was involved). They are the Coinbase and Phantom token pages, a CoinMarketCap page, and a Bitget Wallet X post. The Solayer partnership is described only in the fetched Bitget news piece, with no Solayer program addresses given.

protocol_metadata.about: Bitget SOL (BGSOL) is a liquid staking token issued by the Bitget exchange. Users stake SOL through Bitget's Earn / On-chain Elite product and receive BGSOL. Staking rewards accrue in the SOL/BGSOL exchange rate rather than being paid out. According to Bitget's launch announcement, it was built in partnership with the Solana restaking network Solayer.
